verses.text: The second book of the Prophet Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Azarias, the son of Helchias, the son of Sadamias, the son of Sadoc, the son of Achitob,

The son of Achias, the son of Phinees, the son of Heli, the son of Amarias, the son of Aziei, the son of Marimoth, the son of Arna, the son of Ozias, the son of Borith, the son of Abisei, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar,
The son of Aaron, of the Tribe of Leui, which was captive in the land of the Medes, in the reigne of Artaxerxes king of the Persians.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Go your way, and show my people their sinfull deeds, and their children their wickednes which they have done against me, that they may tell their childrens children,
Because the sins of their fathers are increased in them: for they have forgotten me, and have offered to strange gods.
Am not I even he that brought them out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage? but they have prouoked me to wrath, and despised my counsels.
Pull you off then the haire of your head, and cast all evil upon them, for they have not been obedient to my law, but it is a rebellious people.
How long shall I forbeare them to whom I have done so much good?
Many kings have I destroyed for their sakes, Pharao with his servants, and all his power have I smitten downe.
All the nations have I destroyed before them, and in the East I have scattered the people of two prouinces, even of Tyrus and Sidon, and have slaine all their enemies.
Do you speak therefore to them saying, Thus says the Lord,
I led you through the Sea, and in the beginning gave you a large and safe passage, I gave you Moyses for a leader, and Aaron for a priest,
I gave you light in a pillar of fire, and great wonders have I done among you, yet have you forgotten me, says the Lord.
Thus says the Almightie Lord, The quailes were as a token for you, I gave you tents for your safegard, nevertheless you murmured there,
And triumphed not in my name for the destruction of your enemies, but ever to this day do you yet murmure.
Where are the benefits that I have done for you? when you were hungry and thirstie in the wildernesse, did you not crie to me?
Saying, Why have you brought us into this wildernesse to kill us? It had bin better for us to have served the Egyptians, then to die in this wildernesse.
Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you Manna to eat, so you did eat Angels bread.
When you were thirstie, did I not cleaue the rocke, and waters flowed out to your fill? for the heate I couered you with the leaues of the trees.
I diuided amongst you a fruitfull land, I cast out the Canaanites, the Pherezites, and the Philistines before you: what shall I yet do more for you: says the Lord?
Thus says the Almighty Lord, when you were in the wildernes in the riuer of the Amorites, being athirst, and blaspheming my Name,
I gave you not fire for your blasphemies, but cast a tree in the water, and made the riuer sweet.
What shall I do to you, O Jacob? you Judah would not obey me: I will turne me to other nations, and to those will I give my Name, that they may keep my Statutes.
Seeing you have forsaken me, I will do you forsake also: when you desire me to be gracious to you, I shall have no mercy upon you.
Whensoeuer you shall call upon me, I will not hear you: for you have defiled your hands with blood, and your feete are swift to commit manslaughter.
You have not as it were forsaken me, but your own selues, says the Lord.
Thus says the Almighty Lord, Have I not prayed you as a father his sons, as a mother her daughters, and a nurse her young babes,
That you would be my people, and I shoud be your Alahayam, that you would be my children, and I should be your father?
I gathered you together, as a henne gathers her chickens under her wings: but now, what shall I do to you? I will cast you out from my face.
When you offer to me, I will turne my face from you: for your solemne feast days, your newe Moone, and your circumcisions have I forsaken.
I sent to you my servants the Prophets, whom you have taken and slaine, and torne their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says the Lord.
Thus says the Almighty Lord, Your house is desolate, I will cast you out, as the wind does stubble.
And your children shall not be fruitful: for they have despised my Commandment, and done the thing that is evil before me.
Your houses will I give to a people that shall come, which not having heard of me, yet shall believe me, to whom I have showed no signes, yet they shall do that I have commanded them.
They have seene no Prophets, yet they shall call their sins to remembrance, and acknowledge them.
I take to witnesse the grace of the people to come, whose little ones rejoice in gladnesse: and though they have not seene me with bodily eyes, yet in spirit they believe the thing that I say.
And now brother, behold what glory: and see the people that comes from the East.
Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Oseas, Amos, and Micheas, Ioel, Abdias, and Ionas,
Nahum, and Abacuc, Sophonias, Aggeus, Zacharie, and Malachie, which is called also an Angel of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord, I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them my Commandments by my servants the prophets, whom they would not hear, but despised my counsailes.
The mother that bare them, says to them, Go your way you children, for I am a widow, and forsaken.
I brought you up with gladnesse, but with sorrow and heauinesse have I lost you: for you have sinned before the Lord your Alahayam, and done that thing that is evil before him.
But what shall I now do to you? I am a widow and forsaken: go your way, O my children, and aske mercy of the Lord.
As for me, O father, I call upon you for a witnesse over the mother of these children, which would not keep my Couenant,
That you bring them to confusion, and their mother to a spoile, that there may be no off spring of them.
Let them be scattered abroad among the heathen, let their names be put out of the earth: for they have despised my Couenant.
Woe be to you Assur, you that hidest the unrighteous in you, O you wicked people, remember what I did to Sodome and Gomorrhe.
Whose land lieth in clods of pitch and heapes of ashes: even so also will I do to them that hear me not, says the Almightie Lord.
Thus says the Lord to Esdras, Tell my people that I will give them the kingdom of Hierusalem, which I would have given to Yahsharala.
Their glory also will I take to me, and give these the everlasting Tabernacles, which I had prepared for them.
They shall have the tree of Life for an oyntment of sweet sauour, they shall nether labor, nor be weary.
Go and you shall receive: pray for few days to you, that they may be shortned: the kingdom is already prepared for you: Watch.
Take heaven and earth to witnesse; for I have broken the evil in pieces, and created the good; for I live, says the Lord.
Mother, embrace your children, and bring them up with gladnesse, make their feet as fast as a pillar: for I have chosen you, says the Lord.
And those that be dead will I raise up again from their places, and bring them out of the graues: for I have known my Name in Yahsharala.
Fear not you mother of the children: for I have chosen you, says the Lord.
For your helpe I will send my servants Esay and Ieremie, after whose counsaile I have sanctified and prepared for you twelve trees, laden with diverse fruits;
And as many fountaines flowing with milke and hony: and seven mighty mountaines, whereupon there grow roses and lillies, whereby I will fill your children with ioy.
Do right to the widow, judge for the fatherlesse, give to the poor, defend the orphane, clothe the naked,
Heale the broken and the weake, laugh not a lame man to scorne, defend the maimed, and let the blind man come into the sight of my clearenesse.
Keep the olde and young within your walles.
Wheresouer you find the dead, take them and bury them, and I will give you the first place in my resurrection.
Abide still, O my people, and take your rest, for your quietnesse shall come.
Nourish your children, O you good nource, stablish their feete.
As for the servants whom I have given you, there shall not one of them perish; for I will require them from among your number.
Be not weary, for when the day of trouble and heauinesse comes, others shall weepe and be sorrowfull, but you shall be merry, and have abundance.
The heathen shall enuie you, but they shall be able to do nothing against you, sayth the Lord.
My hands shall couer you, so that your children shall not see hell.
Be ioyfull, O you mother, with your children, for I will deliuer you, sayth the Lord.
Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth, and show mercy to them: for I am mercifull, sayth the Lord Almightie.
Embrace your children until I come and show mercy to them: for my welles runne over, and my grace shall not faile.
I Esdras received a charge of the Lord upon the mount Oreb, that I should go to Yahsharala; but when I came to them, they set me at nought, and despised the commandment of the Lord.
And therefore I say to you, O you heathen, that hear and understand, Look for your shepheard, he shall give you everlasting rest; for he is near at hand, that shall come in the end of the world.
Be ready to the reward of the kingdom, for the everlasting light shall shine upon you for evermore.
Flee the shadow of this world, receive the ioyfulnesse of your glory: I testifie my Sauiour openly.
O receive the gift that is given you, and be glad, giving thankes to him that has called you to the heauenly kingdom.
Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord:
Which are departed from the shadow of the world, and have received glorious garments of the Lord.
Take your number, O Sion, and shut up those of your that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the Law of the Lord.
The number of your children whom you longedst for, is fulfilled: beseech the power of the Lord, that your people which have been called from the beginning, may be hallowed.
I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.
And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller then all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crownes, and was more exalted, which I marueiled at greatly.
So I asked the Angel, and said, Sir, what are these?
He answered, and said to me, These be they that have put off the mortall clothing, and put on the immortall, and have confessed the Name of Alahayam: now are they crowned, and receive palmes.
Then said I to the Angel, What young person is it that crowns them, and gives them palmes in their handes?
So he answered, and said to me, It is the son of Alahayam, whom they have confessed in the world. Then began I greatly to commend them, that stood so stiffely for the Name of the Lord.
Then the Angel said to me, Go your way, and tell my people what manner of things, and how great wonders of the Lord your Alahayam you have seene.
In the thirtieth year after the ruine of the city, I was in Babylon, and lay troubled upon my bed, and my thoughts came up over my heart.
For I saw the desolation of Sion, and the wealth of them that dwelt at Babylon.
And my spirit was sore moved, so that I began to speak words full of fear to the most High, and said,
O Lord, who bear rule, you spoke at the beginning, when you did plant the earth (and that your selfe alone) and commandedst the people,
And gauest a body to Adam without soul, which was the workemanship of your hands, and did breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before you.
And you led him into paradise, which your right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.

And to him you gauest commandment to love your way, which he transgressed, and immediatly you appointedst death in him, and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kinreds out of number.
And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderfull things before you, and despised your commandments.
And again in processe of time you brought the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them.
And it came to pass in every of them, that as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.
Nevertheless one of them you left, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.
And it happened, that when they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, and had gotten them many children, and were a great people, they began again to be more ungodly then the first.
Now when they liued so wickedly before you, you did choose you a man from among them, whose name was Abraham.
Him you louedst, and to him only you shewedst your will:
And madest an everlasting couenant with him, promising him that you would never forsake his seede.
And to him, you gauest Isahac, and to Isahac also you gauest Jacob and Esau. As for Jacob you did choose him to you, and put by Esau: and so Jacob became a great multitude.
And it came to pass, that when you led his seede out of Egypt, you brought them up to the mount Sina.
And bowing the heavens, you didest set fast the earth, mouedst the whole world, and madest the depth to tremble, and troubledst the men of that age.
And your glory went through four gates, of fire, and of earthquake, and of wind, and of cold, that you might give the law to the seed of Jacob, and diligence to the generation of Yahsharala.
And yet took you not away from them a wicked heart, that your law might bring forth fruit in them.
For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are borne of him.
Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law (also) in the heart of the people with the malignity of the roote, so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still.
So the times passed away, and the years were brought to an end: then did you raise you up a servant, called David,
Whom you commandedst to build a city to your name, and to offer incense and oblations to you therein.
When this was done many years, then they that inhabited the city forsooke you,
And in all things did even as Adam, and all his generations had done, for they also had a wicked heart.
And so you gauest the city over into the hands of your enemies.
Are their deeds then any better that inhabite Babylon, that they should therefore have the dominion over Sion?
For when I came there, and had seene impieties without number, then my soul saw many evil doers in this thirtieth year, so that my heart failed me.
For I have seene how you suffer them sinning, and have spared wicked doers: and have destroyed your people, and have preserued your enemies, and have not signified it.
I do not remember how this way may be left: Are they then of Babylon better then they of Sion?
Or is there any other people that knows you besides Yahsharala? or what generation has so believed your Couenants as Jacob?
And yet their reward appears not, and their labor has no fruit: for I have gone here and there through the heathen, and I see that they flowe in wealth, and think not upon your commandments.
Weigh you therfore our wickednesse now in the ballance, and theirs also that dwell in the world: and so shall your Name no where be found, but in Yahsharala.
Or when was it that they which dwell upon the earth, have not sinned in your sight? or what people has so kept your commandments?
You shall find that Yahsharala by name has kept your precepts: but not the heathen.
And the Angel that was sent to me, whose name was Uriel, gave me an answer,
And said, Your heart has gone too farre in this world, and do you think to comprehend the way of the most High?
Then said I, Yea my Lord: and he answered me and said, I am sent to show you three ways, and to set forth three similitudes before you.
Whereof if you can declare me one, I will show you also the way that you desire to see, and I shall show you from whence the wicked heart comes.
And I said, Tel on my Lord. Then said he to me, Go your way, weigh me the weight of the fire, or measure me the blast of the wind, or call me again the day that is past.
Then answered I and said, What man is able to do that, that you should aske such things of me?

And he said to me, If I should aske you how great dwellings are in the midst of the sea, or how many springs are in the beginning of the deepe, or how many springs are above the firmament, or which are the outgoings of Paradise:
Peraduenture you would say to me, I never went downe into the deepe, nor as yet into hell, neither did I ever climbe up into heaven.

Nevertheless, now have I asked you but only of the fire and winde, and of the day where through you have passed, and of things from which you can not be separated, and yet canst you give me uo answeere of them.
He said moreouer to me, Your own things, and such as are growen up with you, canst you not know.
How should your vessel then be able to comprehend the way of the highest, and the world being now outwardly corrupted, to understand the corruption that is euident in my sight?
Then said I to him, It were better that we were not at all, then that we should live still in wickednesse, and to suffer, and not to know why.
He answered me and said, I went into a forest into a plaine, and the trees tooke counsel,
And said, Come, let us go and make war against the Sea, that it may depart away before us, and that we may make us more woods.
The floods of the Sea also in like manner tooke counsel, and said, Come, let us go up and subdue the woods of the plaine, that there also we may make us another country.
The thought of the wood was in vaine, for the fire came and consumed it.
The thought of the floods of the Sea came likewise to nought, for the sand stood up and stopped them.
If you wert judge now betwixt these two, whom would you begin to iustifie, or whom would you condemne?
I answered and said, Uerily it is a foolish thought that they both have deuised: for the ground is given to the wood, and the sea also has his place to beare his floods.
Then answered he me and said, You have given a right iudgment, but why do you judge not your selfe also?

For like as the ground is given to the wood, and the sea to his floods: even so they that dwell upon the earth may understand nothing, but that which is upon the earth: and he that dwells above the heavens, may only understand the things that are above the height of the heavens.
Then answered I, and said, I beseech you, O Lord, let me have understanding.

For it was not my minde to be curious of the high things, but of such as pass by us dayly, namely why Yahsharala is given up as a reproch to the heathen, and for what cause the people whom you have loued, is given over to ungodly nations, and why the Lawe of our forefathers is brought to nought, and the written Couenants come to none effect.
And we pass away out of the world as grassehoppers, and our life is astonishment and fear, and we are not worthy to obtaine mercy.
What will he then do to his Name, whereby we are called? of these things have I asked.
Then answered he me, and said, The more you search, the more you shall marueile, for the world hastens fast to pass away,
And cannot comprehend the things that are promised to the righteous in time to come: for this world is ful of vnrighteousnesse and infirmities.
But as concerning the things whereof you askest me, I will tell you; for the evil is sowen, but the destruction thereof is not yet come.
If therefore that which is sowen, be not turned vpside downe; and if the place where the evil is sowen pass not away, then cannot it come that is sowen with good.

For the graine of evil seed has bene sowen in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much vngodlinesse has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring foorth until the time of threshing come.
Ponder now by your selfe, how great fruit of wickednesse the graine of evil seed has brought forth.
And when the eares shall be cut downe, which are without number, how great a floore shall they fill?
Then I answered and said, How and when shall these things come to pass? why are our years few and evil?
And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vaine to be above him, for you have much exceeded.
Did not the souls also of the righteous aske question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floore of our reward?
And to these things Uriel the Archangel gave them answer, and said, Even when the number of seedes is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the ballance.
By measure has he measured the times, and by number has he numbred the times; and he does not move nor stirre them, until the said measure be fulfilled.
Then answered I, and said, O Lord that bear rule, even we all are full of impietie.
And for our sakes peraduenture it is that the floores of the righteous are not filled, because of the sins of them that dwell upon the earth.
So he answered me, and said, Go your way to a wman with childe, and aske of her, when she has fulfilled her nine moneths, if her wombe may keep the birth any longer within her?
Then said I, No Lord, that can she not. And he said to me, In the graue, the chambers of souls are like the wombe of a woman:
For like as a woman in labor, makes haste to escape the pains of childbirth: even so do these places haste to deliuer those things that are committed to them.
From the beginning look what you desire to see, it shalbe showed you.
Then answered I, and said, If I have found favor in your sight, and if it be possible, and if I be meet therefore,
Show me then whether there be more to come then is past, or more past then is to come.
What is past I know; but what is for to come I know not.
And he said to me, Stand up upon the right side, and I shall expound the similitude to you.
So I stood and saw, and behold an hot burning ouen passed by before me: and it happened that when the flame was gone by, I looked, and behold, the smoke remained still.
After this there passed by before me a watrie cloude, and sent downe much raine with a storme, and when the stormie raine was past, the drops remained still.

Then said he to me, Consider with your selfe: as the raine is more then the drops, and as the fire is greater then the smoke: but the drops and the smoke remain behind: so the quantity which is past, did more exceede.
Then I prayed, and said, May I live, do you think, until that time? or what shall happen in those days?
He answered me, and said, As for the tokens whereof you askest me, I may tell you of them in part; but as touching your life, I am not sent to show you, for I do not know it.

Neuertheles as concerning the tokens, beholde, the days shall come that they which dwell upon earth, shall be taken in a great number, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.
But iniquitie shalbe increased above that which now you seest, or that you have heard long agoe.
And the land that you seest now to have roote, shall you see wasted suddenly.
But if the most high graunt you to live, you shall see after the third trumpet, that the Sunne shall suddenly shine again in the night, and the Moone thrice in the day.
And blood shall drop out of wood, and the stone shall give his voice, and the people shalbe troubled.
And enen he shall rule whom they look not for that dwel upon the earth, and the foules shall take their flight away together.
And the Sodomitish sea shall cast out fish, and make a noyse in the night, which many have not known: but they shall all hear the voice thereof.
There shall be a confusion also in many places, and the fire shalbe oft sent out again, and the wilde beasts shall change their places, and menstruous women shall bring foorth monsters.
And salt waters shall be found in the sweete, and all friends shall destroy one another: then shall wit hide it selfe, and understanding withdraw it selfe into his secret chamber,
And shall be sought of many, and yet not be found: then shall vnrighteousnesse and incontinencie be multiplyed upon earth.
One land also shall aske another, and say, Is righteousnes that makes a man righteous, gone through you? And it shall say, No.
At the same time shall men hope, but nothing obtaine: they shall labor, but their ways shall not prosper.
To show you such tokens I have leave: and if you will pray again, and weepe as now, and fast seven days, you shall hear yet greater things.
Then I awaked, and an extreme fearefulnesse went through all my body, and my minde was troubled, so that it fainted.
So the Angel that was come to talke with me, helde me, comforted me, and set me up upon my feete.
And in the second night it came to pass, that Salathiel the captaine of the people came to me, saying, Where have you been? and why is your countenance so heauie?
Do you know not that Yahsharala is committed to you, in the land of their captiuitie?
Up then, and eat bread, and forsake us not as the shepheard that leaves his flocke in the handes of cruell wolues.
Then said I to him, Go your waies from me, and come not near me: And he heard what I said, and went from me.
And so I fasted seven days, monrning and weeping, like as Uriel the Angel commanded me.
And after seven days, so it was that the thoughts of my heart were very grieuous to me again.
And my soul recouered the spirit of understanding, and I began to talke with the most high again,
And said, O Lord, that bear rule of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine.
And of all lands of the whole world you have chosen you one pit: and of all the flowers thereof, one Lillie.
And of all the depths of the Sea, you have filled you one riuer: and of all builded cities, you have hallowed Sion to your selfe.
And of all the foules that are created, you have named you one Doue: and of all the cattell that are made, you have prouided you one sheepe.
And among all the multitudes of peoples, you have gotten you one people: and to this people whom you louedst, you gauest a law that is approued of all.
And now O Lord, why have you given this one people over to many? and upon the one roote have you prepared others, and why have you scattered your only one people among many?
And they which did gainesay your promises, and believed not your couenants, have trodden them downe.
If you did so much hate your people, yet should you punish them with your own hands.
Now when I had spoken these words, the Angell that came to me the night afore, was sent to me,
And said to me, Hear me, and I will instruct you, hearken to the thing that I say, and I shall tell you more.
And I said, Speak on, my Lord: then said he to me, you are sore troubled in minde for Israels sake: louest you that people better then he that made them?
And I said, No Lord, but of very griefe have I spoken: For my reines paine me every houre, while I labor to comprehend the way of the most High, and to seeke out part of his judgment.

And he said to me, You can not: and I said, wherfore Lord? wherunto was I borne then? or why was not my mothers wombe then my graue, that I might not have seene the trauell of Jacob, and the wearisome toyle of the stocke of Yahsharala?
And he said to me, Number me the things that are not yet come, gather me together the droppes that are scattered abroad, make me the flowres greene again that are withered.
Open me the places that are closed, and bring me forth the winds that in them are shut up, show me the image of a voyce: and then I will declare to you the thing that you labor to know.
And I said, O Lord, that bear rule, who may know these things, but he that has not his dwelling with men?
As for me, I am vnwise: how may I then speak of these things whereof you askest me?
Then said he to me, Like as you can do none of these things that I have spoken of, even so canst you not find out my judgment, or in the end the love that I have promised to my people.
And I said, behold, O Lord, yet art you near to them that be reserued until the end; and what shall they do that have been before me, or we (that be now) or they that shall come after us?
And he said to me, I will liken my judgment to a ring: like as there is no slacknesse of the last, even so there is no swiftnesse of the first.
So I answered and said, Couldst you not make those that have been made, and be now, and that are for to come, at once, that you might shewe your judgment the sooner?
Then answered he me, and said, The creature may not have above the maker, neither may the world hold them at once that shalbe created therin.

And I said, As you have said to your servant, that you which giuest life to all, have given life at once to the creature that you have created, and the creature bare it: even so it might now also beare them that now be present at once.
And he said to me, Aske the wombe of a woman, and say to her, If you bring forth children, why do you it not together, but one after another? pray her therefore to bring forth tenne children at once.
And I said, She cannot: but must do it by distance of time.
Then said he to me, Even so have I given the wombe of the earth to those that be sowen in it, in their times.
For like as a young child may not bring forth the things that belong to the aged, even so have I disposed the world which I created.
And I asked and said, Seeing you have now given me the way, I will proceed to speak before you: for our mother of whom you have told me that she is young, draws now near to age.
He answered me and said, Aske a woman that bears children, and she shall tell you.
Say to her, Why are not they whome you have now brought forth, like those that were before, but lesse of stature?
And she shall answer you, They that be borne in the strength of youth, are of one fashion, and they that are borne in the time of age (when the wombe fails) are otherwise.
Consider you therfore also, how that you are lesse of stature then those that were before you.
And so are they that come after you lesse then you, as the creatures which now begin to be old, and have passed over the strength of youth.
Then saide I, Lord, I beseech you, if I have found fauor in your sight, show your servant by whom you visit your creature.
And he said to me, in the beginning when the earth was made, before the borders of the world stood, or ever the windes blew,
Before it thundred and lightned, or ever the foundations of Paradise were laide,
Before the faire flowers were seene, or ever the moueable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of Angels were gathered together,
Or ever the heights of the aire were lifted up, before the measures of the firmament were named, or ever the chimnies in Sion were hot,
And ere the present years were sought out, and or ever the inuentions of them that now sin were turned, before they were sealed that have gathered faith for a treasure:
Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.
Then answered I and said, What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the ende of the first, and the beginning of it that follows?
And he said to me, From Abraham to Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were borne of him, Iacobs hand held first the heele of Esau.
For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that follows.
The hand of man is betwixt the heele and the hand: other question, Esdras, aske you not.
¶ I answered then and said, O Lord that bear rule, if I have found favor in your sight,
I beseech you, show your servant the end of your tokens, whereof you shewedst me part the last night.
So he answered and said to me, Stand up upon your feete, and hear a mighty sounding voyce.
And it shall be as it were a great motion, but the place where you stand, shall not be moved.
And therefore when it speaks be not afraid: for the word is of the end, and the foundation of the earth is understood.
And why? because the speech of these things trembles and is mooued: for it knows that the ende of these things must be changed.
And it happened that when I had heard it, I stood up upon my feet, and hearkened, and behold, there was a voice that spoke, and the sound of it was like the sound of many waters.
And it said, Behold, the days come, that I will begin to draw near, and to visit them that dwell upon the earth,
And will begin to make inquisition of them, what they be that have hurt vniustly with their vnrighteousnesse, and when the affliction of Sion shalbe fulfilled.
And when the world that shall begin to vanish away shall be finished: then will I show these tokens, the books shalbe opened before the firmament, and they shall see all together.
And the children of a year olde shall speak with their voyces, the women with childe shall bring foorth vntimely children, of three or four moneths old: and they shall live, and be raised up.
And suddenly shall the sowen places appeare vnsowen, the full storehouses shall suddenly be found empty.
And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man hears they shalbe suddenly afraid.

At that time shall friendes fight one against another like enemies, and the earth shall stand in fear with those that dwell therein, the springs of the fountaines shall stand still, and in three houres they shall not runne.
Whoever remains from all these that I have told you, shall escape, and see my saluation, and the ende of your world.
And the men that are received, shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth: and the heart of the inhabitants shalbe changed, and turned into another meaning.
For evil shalbe put out, and deceit shalbe quenched.
As for faith, it shall flourish, corruption shalbe overcome, and the truth which has bene so long without fruit, shalbe declared.
And when he talked with me, behold, I looked by little and little upon him before whom I stood.
And these words said he to me, I am come to show you the time of the night to come.
If you will pray yet more, and fast seven days again, I shall tel you greater things by day, then I have heard.
For your voice is heard before the most High: for the mighty has seene your righteous dealing, he has seene also your chastitie, which you have had ever since your youth.
And therefore has he sent me to show you al these things, and to say to you, Be of good comfort, and fear not.
And hasten not with the times that are past, to thinke vaine things, that you may not hasten from the latter times.
And it came to pass after this, that I wept again, and fasted seven days in like manner, that I might fulfill the three weekes which he told me.
And in the eight night was my heart vexed within me again, and I began to speak before the most High.
For my spirit was greatly set on fire, and my soul was in distresse.
And I said, O Lord, you spoke from the beginning of the creation, even the first day, and said thus, Let heaven and earth be made: and your word was a perfect worke.
And then was the spirit, and darkenesse, and silence were on every side; the sound of mans voice was not yet formed.
Then commandedst you a faire light to come foorth of your treasures, that your worke might appeare.
Upon the second day you madest the spirit of the firmament, and commandedst it to part asunder, and to make a diuision betwixt the waters, that the one part might go up, and the other remain beneath.

Upon the thirde day you did commaund that the waters should be gathered in the seventh part of the earth: six parts have you dried up and kept them, to the intent that of these some being planted of Alahayam and tilled, might serve you.
For as soone as your word went foorth, the worke was made.

For immediatly there was great and innumerable fruit, and many and diverse pleasures for the taste, and flowers of vnchangeable colour, and odours of wonderfull smell: and this was done the third day.
Upon the fourth day you commandedst that the Sunne should shine, and the Moone give her light, and the starres should be in order,
And gauest them a charge to do seruice to man, that was to be made.
Upon the fift day, you saydst to the seventh part, where the waters were gathered, that it should bring foorth living creatures, foules and fishes: and so it came to pass.
For the dumbe water, and without life, brought foorth living things at the commandment of Alahayam, that al people might praise your wondrous works.
Then did you ordeine two living creatures, the one you calledst Enoch, and the other Leuiathan,
And did separate the one from the other: for the seventh part (namely where the water was gathered together) might not hold them both.
Unto Enoch you gauest one part which was dried up the third day, that he should dwel in the same part, wherein are a thousand hilles.
But to Leuiathan you gauest the seventh part, namely the moist, and have kept him to be deuoured of whom you will, and when.
Upon the sixt day you gauest commandment to the earth, that before you it should bring foorth beasts, cattell, and creeping things:
And after these, Adam also whom you madest lord of all your creatures, of him come we all, and the people also whom you have chosen.
All this have I spoken before you, O Lord, because you madest the world for our sakes.
As for the other people which also come of Adam, you have said that they are nothing, but be like to spittle, and have likened the abundance of them to a drop that falls from a vessell.
And now, O Lord, behold, these heathen, which have ever been reputed as nothing, have begun to be lordes over us, and to deuoure us:
But we your people (whom you have called your first borne, your only begotten, and your feruent louer) are given into their hands.
If the world now be made for our sakes, why do we not possesse an inheritance with the world? how long shall this endure?
And when I had made an ende of speaking these words, there was sent to me the Angel which had been sent to me the nights afore.
And he said to me, Up Esdras, and hear the words that I am come to tell you.
And I said, Speak on, my Alahayam. Then said he to me, The Sea is set in a wide place, that it might be deepe and great.
But put the case the entrance were narrow, and like a riuer,
Who then could go into the Sea to look upon it, and to rule it? If he went not through the narrow, how could he come into the broad?
There is also another thing. A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things.
The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deepe water.
And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.
If this city now were given to a man for an inheritance, if he never shall pass the danger set before it, how shall he receive this inheritance?
And I said, It is so, Lord. Then said he to me, Even so also is Israels portion:
Because for their sakes I made the world: and when Adam transgressed my Statutes, then was decreed that now is done.
Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and hardship: they are but few and evil, full of perils, and very painefull.
For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortall fruit.
If then they that live, labor not to enter these strait and vaine things, they can never receive those that are laide up for them.
Now therefore why disquiet you your selfe, seeing you are but a corruptible man? and why art you mooued, whereas you are but mortall?
Why have you not considered in your minde this thing that is to come, rather then that which is present?
Then answered I, and said, O Lord, that bear rule, you have ordained in your Law, that the righteous should inherite these things, but that the ungodly should perish:
Nevertheless, the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly, have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.
And he said to me, There is no judge above Alahayam, and none that has understanding above the highest.
For there be many that perish in this life, because they despise the Lawe of Alahayam that is set before them.
For Alahayam has given strait commandment to such as came, what they should do to live, even as they came, and what they should obserue to auoid punishment.
Nevertheless they were not obedient to him, but spoke against him, and imagined vaine things:
And deceiued themselues by their wicked deeds, and said of the most Hie, that he is not, and knew not his waies.
But his Law have they despised, and denied his couenants in his statutes have they not been faithfull, and have not performed his workes.
And therfore Esdras, for the emptie, are emptie things, and for the ful, are the full things.
Behold, the time shall come, that these tokens which I have told you, shall come to pass, and the bride shall appeare, and she comming forth shall be seene, that now is withdrawen from the earth.
And whoever is deliuered from the foresaid evils, shall see my wonders.
For my son Yahawashi shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.
After these years shall my son Christ die, and all men that have life.
And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former iudgements: so that no man shall remain.
And after seven days, the world that yet awakens not shall be raised up, and that shall die, that is corrupt.
And the earth shall restore those that are asleepe in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliuer those souls that were committed to them.
And the most high shall appeare upon the seate of judgment, and miserie shall pass away, and the long suffering shall have an end.
But judgment only shall remain, truth shall stand, and faith shall waxe strong.
And the worke shall follow, and the reward shall be showed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall beare no rule.
Then said I, Abraham prayed first for the Sodomites, and Moses for the fathers that sinned in the wildernesse:
And Joshua after him for Yahsharala in the time of Achan,
And Samuel; and David for the destruction: and Solomon for them that should come to the sanctuary.
And Helias for those that received raine, and for the dead that he might live.
And Ezechias for the people in the time of Sennacherib: and many for many.
Even so now seeing corruption is growen up, and wickednesse increased, and the righteous have prayed for the ungodly: why shall it not be so now also?
He answered me and said, This present life is not the end where much glory does abide; therefore have they prayed for the weake.
But the day of doome shall be the end of this time, and the beginning of the immortality for to come, wherein corruption is past.
Intemperancie is at an end, infidelity is cut off, righteousness is growen, and truth is sprung up.
Then shall no man be able to saue him that is destroyed, nor to oppresse him that has gotten the victory.
I answered then and said, This is my first and last saying; that it had been better not to have given the earth to Adam: or else when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.
For what profit is it for men now in this present time to live in heauinesse, and after death to look for punishment?
O you Adam, what have you done? for though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.
For what profit is it to us, if there be promised us an immortall time, wheras we have done the works that bring death?
And that their is promised us an everlasting hope, whereas our selues being most wicked are made vaine?
And that there are layd up for us dwellings of health and safety, whereas we have liued wickedly?
And that the glory of the most high is kept to defend them which have led a wary life, whereas we have walked in the most wicked ways of all?
And that there should be showed a paradise whose fruit endures for ever, wherein is securitie and medicine, sith we shall not enter into it?
For we have walked in vnpleasant places.
And that the faces of them which have used abstinence, shall shine above the starres, whereas our faces shall be blacker then darkenesse?
For while we liued and committed iniquitie, we considered not that we should begin to suffer for it after death.
Then answered he me and saide, This is the condition of the battell, which man that is borne upon the earth shall fight,
That if he be overcome, he shall suffer as you have said, but if he get the victorie, he shall receive the thing that I say.
For this is the life whereof Moses spoke to the people while he liued, saying, Choose you life that you may live.
Nevertheless they believed not him, nor yet the prophets after him, no nor me which have spoken to them,
That there should not be such heauinesse in their destruction, as shall be ioy over them that are persuaded to saluation.
I answered then and saide, I know, Lord, that the most Hie is called mercifull, in that he has mercy upon them, which are not yet come into the world,
And upon those also that turne to his Law,
And that he is patient, and long suffers those that have sinned, as his creatures,
And that he is bountifull, for he is ready to give where it needs,
And that is of great mercy, for he multiplies more and more mercies to them that are present, and that are past, and also to them which are to come.
For if he shall not multiplie his mercies, the world would not continue with them that inherit therein.
And he pardons; for if he did not so of his goodness, that they which have committed iniquities might be eased of them, the ten thousand part of men should not remain living.
And being Judge, if he should not forgiue them that are cured with his word, and put out the multitude of contentions,
There should be very fewe left peraduenture in an innumerable multitude.
And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for fewe.

I will tell you a similitude, Esdras, As when you askest the earth, it shall say to you, that it gives much mold wherof earthen vessels are made, but litle dust that golde comes of: even so is the course of this present world.
There be many created, but few shall be saued.
So answered I and said, Swallow then downe O my soul, understanding, and deuoure wisdom.
For you have agreed to give eare, and art willing to prophesie: for you have no longer space then only to live.

O Lord, if you suffer not your servant that we may pray before you, and you give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it, howe shall each man live that is corrupt, who bears the place of a man?
For you are alone, and we all one workemanship of your hands, like as you have said.

For when the body is fashioned now in the mothers wombe, and you giuest it members, your creature is preserued in fire and water, and nine months does your workemanship endure your creature which is created in her.
But that which keeps, and is kept, shall both be preserued: and when the time comes, the wombe preserued, delivers up the things that grew in it.
For you have commanded out of the parts of the body, that is to say, out of the breasts milke to be given, which is the fruit of the breasts,
That the thing which is fashioned, may be nourished for a time, until you dispose it to your mercy.
You brought it up with your righteousness, and nourturedst it in your Law, and reformedst it with your judgment.
And you shall mortifie it as your creature, and quicken it as your worke.
If therefore you shall destroy him which with so great labor was fashioned, it is an easie thing to be ordained by your Commandment, that the thing which was made might be preserued.
Now therefore, Lord, I will speak (touchiug man in generall, you know best) but touching your people, for whose sake I am sory,
And for your inheritance, for whose cause I mourne, and for Yahsharala, for whom I am heauy, and for Jacob, for whose sake I am troubled:
Therefore will I begin to pray before you, for my selfe, and for them: for I see the falles of us that dwell in the land.
But I have heard the swiftnesse of the Judge which is to come.
Therefore hear my voyce, and understand my words, and I shall speak before you: this is the beginning of the words of Esdras, before he was taken up: and I said;
O Lord, You that dwell in euerlastingnes, which behold from above, things in the heaven, and in the aire,
Whose Throne is inestimable, whose glory may not be comprehended, before whom the hosts of Angels stand with trembling,
(Whose seruice is conuersant in wind and fire,) whose word is true, and sayings constant, whose Commandment is strong, and ordinance fearefull,
Whose look drieth up the depths, and indignation makes the mountaines to melt away, which the truth witnesses:
O hear the prayer of your servant, and give eare to the petition of your creature.
For while I live, I will speak, and so long as I have understanding, I will answer.
O look not upon the sins of your people: but on them which serve you in truth.
Regard not the wicked inuentions of the heathen: but the desire of those that keep your Testimonies in afflictions.
Thinke not upon those that have walked fainedly before you: but remember them, which according to your will have known your fear.
Let it not be your will to destroy them, which have liued like beasts: but to look upon them that have clearely taught your Law.
Do you take no indignation at them which are deemed worse then beasts: but love them that alway put their trust in your righteousness, and glory.
For we and our fathers do languish of such diseases; but because of us sinners, you shall be called mercifull.
For if you have a desire to have mercy upon us, you shall be called mercifull, to us namely, that have no workes of righteousness.
For the just which have many good workes layed up with you, shall out of their own deeds receive reward.
For what is man that you should take displeasure at him? or what is a corruptible generation, that you should be so bitter toward it?
For in truth there is no man among them that be borne, but he has dealt wickedly, and among the faithfull, there is none which has not done amisse.
For in this, O Lord, your righteousness, and your goodness shalbe declared, if you be mercifull to them which have not the confidence of good workes.
Then answered he me, and said, Some things have you spoken aright, and according to your words it shalbe.
For indeed I will not thinke on the disposition of them which have sinned before death, before judgment, before destruction.
But I will rejoice over the disposition of the righteous, and I will remember also their pilgrimage, and the saluation, and the reward that they shall have.
Like as I have spoken now, so shall it come to pass.

For as the husbandmau soweth much seed upon the ground, and plants many trees, and yet the thing that is sowen good in his season, comes not up, neither does all that is planted take root: even so is it of them that are sowen in the world, they shall not all be saued.
I answered then, and said, If I have found grace, let me speak.
Like as the husbandmans seede perishes, if it come not up, and receive not the raine in due season, or if there come too much raine and corrupt it:

Even so perishes man also which is formed with your hands, and is called your own image, because you are like to him, for whose sake you have made all things, and likened him to the husbandmans seede.
Be not wroth with us, but spare your people, and have mercy upon your own inheritance: for you are mercifull to your creature.
Then answered he me, and said, Things present are for the present, and things to come, for such as be to come.
For you come farre short, that you should be able to love my creature more then I: but I have oft times drawen near to you, and to it, but never to the unrighteous.
In this also you are marueilous before the most high;
In that you have humbled your selfe as it becomes you, and have not iudged your selfe worthy to be much glorified among the righteous.
For many great miseries shall be done to them, that in the latter time shall dwell in the world, because they have walked in great pride.
But understand you for your selfe, and seeke out the glory for such as be like you.
For to you is Paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousnesse is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea perfect goodness and wisdom.
The root of evil is sealed up from you, weakenesse and the moth is hidde from you, and corruption is fled into hell to be forgotten.
Sorrows are passed, and in the end is showed the treasure of immortalitie.
And therefore aske you no more questions concerning the multitude of them that perish.
For when they had taken liberty, they despised the most High, thought scorne of his Lawe, and forsooke his ways.
Moreouer, they have troden downe his righteous,
And said in their heart, that there is no Alahayam, yea and that knowing they must die.
For as the things aforesaid shall receive you, so thirst and paine are prepared for them; for it was not his will that men should come to nought.
But they which be created, have defiled the Name of him that made them, and were vnthankefull to him which prepared life for them.
And therefore is my judgment now at hand.
These things have I not showed to all men, but to you, and a fewe like you. Then answered I, and said,
Behold, O Lord, now have you showed me the multitude of the wonders which you will begin to do in the last times: but at what time, you have not showed me.
He answered me then, and sayde, Measure you the time diligently in it selfe: and when you seest part of the signes past, which I have tolde you before,
Then shall you understand, that it is the very same time, wherein the highest will begin to visite the world which he made.
Therefore when there shall be seene earthquakes and vprores of the people in the world:
Then shall you wel understand, that the most high spoke of those things from the days that were before you, even from the beginning.
For like as all that is made in the world has a beginning, and an ende, and the end is manifest:
Even so the times also of the highest, have plaine beginnings in wonders and powerfull workes, and endings in effects and signes.
And every one that shalbe saued, and shalbe able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby you have believed,
Shall be preserued from the said perils, and shall see my saluation, in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me, from the beginning.
Then shall they be in pitifull case which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away desspitefully, shall dwell in torments.
For such, as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me:
And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it:
The same must know it after death by paine.
And therefore be you not curious, how the ungodly shalbe punished and when: but enquire how the righteous shall be saued, whose the world is, and for whom the world is created.
Then answered I, and said,
I have said before, and now do speak, and will speak it also heereafter: that there be many moe of them which perish, then of them which shall be saued,
Like as a waue is greater then a droppe.

And he answered me, saying: like as the field is, so is also the seed: as the flowres be, such are the colours also: such as the workeman is, such also is the worke: and as the husbandman is himselfe, so is his husbandry also: for it was the time of the world.
And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spoke against me.
For then every one obeyed, but now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made, are corrupted by a perpetuall seed, and by a law which is vnsearchable, rid themselues.
So I considered the world, and behold there was perill, because of the deuices that were come into it.
And I saw and spared it greatly, and have kept me a grape of the cluster, and a plant of a great people.
Let the multitude perish then, which was borne in vaine, and let my grape be kept and my plant: for with great labor have I made it perfect.
Nevertheless if you will cease yet seven days moe (but you shall not fast in them.)
But go into a field of flowres, where no house is builded, and eat only the flowres of the field, Tast no flesh, drinke no wine, but eat flowres only.
And pray to the Highest continually, then will I come and talke with you.
So I went my way into the field which is called Ardath, like as he commanded me, and there I sate amongst the flowres, and did eat of the herbes of the field, and the food of the same satisfied me.
After seven days I sate upon the grasse, and my heart was vexed within me, like as before.
And I opened my mouth, and began to talke before the most High and said,
O Lord, you that show your selfe to us, you were showed to our fathers in the wildernesse, in a place where no man treads, in a barren place when they came out of Egypt.
And you spoke, saying, Hear me, O Yahsharala, and marke my words, you seed of Jacob.
For behold I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honored in it for ever.
But our fathers which received the law, kept it not, and obserued not your ordinances, and though the fruit of your law did not perish, neither could it, for it was yours:
Yet they that received it, perished, because they kept not the thing that was sowen in them.
And loe, it is a custome when the ground has received seed, or the Sea a ship, or any vessel, food or drinke, that, that being perished wherein it was sowen, or cast into,
That thing also which was sowen or cast therein, or received, does perish, and remains not with us: but with us it has not happened so.
For we that have received the law perish by sin, and our heart also which received it.
Notwithstanding the law perishes not, but remains in his force.

And when I spoke these things in my heart, I looked backe with mine eyes, and upon the right side I saw a woman, and behold, she mourned, and wept with a loud voyce, and was much grieved in heart, and her clothes were rent, and she had ashes upon her head.
Then let I my thoughts go that I was in, and turned me to her,
And said to her, Why do you weep? why art you so grieved in your minde?
And she said to me, Sir, let me alone, that I may bewaile my selfe, and adde to my sorow, for I am sore vexed in my minde, and brought very low.
And I said to her, What aileth you? Tell me.
She said to me, I your servant have bene barren, and had no childe, though I had an husband thirty yeres.
And those thirty years I did nothing else day and night, and every houre, but make my prayer to the highest.

After thirty years, Alahayam heard me your handmaid, looked upon my misery, considered my trouble, and gave me a son: and I was very glad of him, so was my husband also, and all my neighbours, and we gave great honor to the Almightie.
And I nourished him with great effort.
So when he grew up, and came to the time that he should have a wife, I made a feast.
And it so came to pass, that when my son was entred into his wedding chamber, he fell downe and died.
Then we all ouerthrew the lights, and all my neighbours rose up to comfort me, so I tooke my rest to the second day at night.
And it came to pass when they had all left off to comfort me, to the end I might be quiet: then rose I up by night and fled, and came here into this field, as you seest.
And I do now purpose not to returne into the city, but here to stay, and neither to eat nor drinke, but continually to mourne, and to fast vntil I die.
Then left I the meditations wherein I was, and spoke to her in anger, saying,
You foolish woman above all other, seest you not our mourning, and what happens to us?
How that Sion our mother is full of all heauinesse, and much humbled, mourning very sore?
And now seeing we all mourne, and are sad, for we are all in heauinesse, art you grieved for one son?
For aske the earth, and she shall tell you, that it is she, which ought to mourne, for the fall of so many that grow upon her.
For out of her came all at the first, and out of her shall all others come: and behold they walk almost all into destruction, and a multitude of them is vtterly rooted out.
Who then should make more mourning, then she that has lost so great a multitude, and not you which art sory but for one?
But if you sayest to me, My lamentation is not like the earths, because I have lost the fruit of my womb, which I brought foorth with paines, and bare with sorrowes.
But the earth not so: for the multitude present in it, according to the course of the earth, is gone, as it came.
Then say I to you, Like as you have brought foorth with labor: even so the earth also has given her fruit, namely man, ever sithence the beginning, to him that made her.
Now therefore keep your sorrow to your selfe, and beare with a good courage that which has befallen you.
For if you shall acknowledge the determination of Alahayam to be just, you shall both receive your son in time, and shall be commended amongst women.
Go your way then into the city, to your husband.
And she said to me, That will I not do: I will not go into the city, but here will I die.
So I proceeded to speak further to her, and said,
Do not so, but be counselled by me: for how many are the aduersities of Sion? Be comforted in regard of the sorow of Jerusalem.
For you seest that our Sanctuary is laid waste, our Altar broken downe, our Temple destroyed.

Our Psaltery is laid on the ground, our song is put to silence, our reioycing is at an end, the light of our candlesticke is put out, the Arke of our Couenant is spoiled, our holy things are defiled, and the Name that is called upon us, is almost prophaned: our children are put to shame, our priests are burnt, our Levites are gone into captiuitie, our virgines are defiled, and our wiues rauished, our righteous men caried away, our litle ones destroyed, our young men are brought in bondage, and our strong men are become weake.
And which is the greatest of all, the seale of Sion has now lost her honor: for she is deliuered into the hands of them that hate us.
And therefore shake off your great heauinesse, and put away the multitude of sorrowes, that the mighty may be mercifull to you again, and the highest shall give you rest, and ease from your labor.
And it came to pass while I was talking with her, behold her face upon a sudden shined exceedingly, and her countenance glistered, so that I was afraid of her, and mused what it might be.
And behold suddenly, she made a great cry very fearful: so that the earth shooke at the noise of the woman.

And I looked, and beholde, the woman appeared to me no more, but there was a city builded, and a large place showed it selfe from the foundations: then was I afraid, and cried with a lowd voice, and said,
Where is Uriel the Angel, who came to me at the first? for he has caused me to fall into many traunces, and mine end is turned into corruption, and my prayer to rebuke.
And as I was speaking these words, behold, he came to me, and looked upon me.
And loe, I lay as one that had bene dead, and mine understanding was taken from me, and he tooke me by the right hand, and comforted me, and set me upon my feet, and said to me,
What aileth you? and why art you so disquieted, and why is yours understanding troubled, and the thoughts of your heart?
And I said, because you have forsaken me, and yet I did according to your words, and I went into the field, and loe I have seene, and yet see, that I am not able to expresse.
And he said to me, Stand up manfully, and I will aduise you.
Then said I, Speak on, my lord in me, only forsake me not, lest I die frustrate of my hope.
For I have seene, that I knew not, and hear that I do not know.
Or, is my sense deceiued, or my soul in a dreame?
Now therfore, I beseech you, that you will show your servant of this vision.
He answered me then, and said, Hear me, and I shall enforme you, and tell you why you are afraid: for the highest will reueile many secret things to you.
He has seene that your way is right: for that you sorrow continually for your people, and makest great lamentation for Sion.
This therefore is the meaning of the vision which you lately sawest.
You sawest a woman mourning, and you beganst to comfort her:
But now seest you the likenesse of the woman no more, but there appeared to you a city builded.
And whereas she told you of the death of her son, this is the solution.
This woman whom you sawest, is Sion: and whereas she said to you (even she whom you seest as a city builded.)
Whereas I say, she said to you, that she has bene thirty yeres barren: those are the thirty years wherein there was no offering made in her.
But after thirty years, Solomon builded the city, and offered offrings: and then bare the barren a son.
And whereas she told you that she nourished him with labor: that was the dwelling in Hierusalem.
But whereas she said to you, That my son comming into his marriage chamber, happened to have a fall, and died, this was the destruction that came to Hierusalem.
And behold, you sawest her likenesse, and because she mourned for her son, you beganst to comfort her, and of these things which have chaunced, these are to be opened to you.
For now the most High seeth, that you are grieved vnfainedly, and suffer from your whole heart for her, so has he showed you the brightnes of her glory, and the comelinesse of her beautie.
And therfore I bad you remain in the field, where no house was builded.
For I knew that the Highest would show this to you.
Therefore I commanded you to go into the field, where no foundation of any building was.
For in the place wherein the Highest begins to show his city, ther can no mans building be able to stand.
And therfore fear not, let not your heart be afrighted, but go your way in, and see the beautie and greatnesse of the building, as much as your eyes be able to see:
And then shall you hear as much as your eares may comprehend.
For you are blessed above many other, and art called with the highest, and so are but few.
But to morrow at night you shall remain here.
And so shall the highest show you visions of the high things, which the most high will do to them, that dwel upon earth in the last days. So I slept that night and another, like as he commanded me.
Then saw I a dreame, and beholde, there came up from the Sea an Eagle, which had twelve feathered wings, and three heads.
And I saw, and behold, she spred her wings over all the earth, and all the windes of the ayre blewe on her, and were gathered together.
And I beheld, and out of her feathers there grewe other contrary feathers, and they became little feathers, and small.
But her heads were at rest: the head in the midst was greater then the other, yet rested it with the residue.
Moreouer I beheld, and loe, the Eagle flew with her feathers, and reigned upon earth, and over them that dwelt therein.
And I saw that all things under heaven were subiect to her, and no man spoke against her, no not one creature upon earth.
And I beheld, and loe, the Eagle rose upon her talents, and spoke to her feathers, saying,
Watch not all at once, sleepe every one in his own place, and watch by course.
But let the heads be preserued for the last.
And I beheld, and loe, the voice went not out of her heads, but from the midst of her body.
And I numbred her contrary feathers, and behold, there were eight of them.
And I looked, and behold, on the right side there arose one feather, and reigned over all the earth.
And so it was, that when it reigned, the ende of it came, and the place thereof appeared no more: so the next following stood up and reigned, and had a great time.
And it happened, that when it reigned, the end of it came also, like as the first, so that it appeared no more.
Then came there a voice to it, and said,
Hear, you that have borne rule over the earth so long: this I say to you, before you begin to appeare no more.
There shall none after you attaine to your time, neither to the halfe thereof.
Then arose the third, and reigned as the other before: and appeared no more also.
So went it with all the residue one after another, as that every one reigned, and then appeared no more.
Then I beheld, and loe, in processe of time, the feathers that folowed, stood up upon the right side, that they might rule also, and some of them ruled, but within a while they appeared no more:
For some of them were set up, but ruled not.
After this I looked, and behold, the twelve feathers appeared no more, nor the two little feathers:
And there was no more upon the Eagles body, but three heads that rested, and six little wings.
Then saw I also that two little feathers diuided themselues from the six, and remained under the head, that was upon the right side: for the four continued in their place.
And I beheld, and loe, the feathers that were under the wing, thought to set up themselues, and to have the rule.
And I beheld, and loe, there was one set up, but shortly it appeared no more.
And the second was sooner away then the first.
And I beheld, and loe, the two that remained, thought also in themselues to reigne.
And when they so thought, behold, there awaked one of the heads that were at rest, namely it that was in the midst, for that was greater then the two other heads.
And then I saw, that the two other heads were ioyned with it.
And behold, the head was turned with them that were with it, and did eat up the two feathers under the wing that would have reigned.

But this head put the whole earth in fear, and bare rule in it over all those that dwelt upon the earth, with much oppression, and it had the gouernance of the world more then all the wings that had been.
And after this I beheld, and loe the head that was in the midst, suddenly appeared no more, like as the wings.
But there remained the two heads, which also in like sort ruled upon the earth, and over those that dwelt therein.
And I beheld, and loe, the head upon the right side, deuoured it, that was upon the left side.
Then I heard a voyce, which said to me, Look before you, and consider the thing that you seest.
And I beheld, and loe, as it were a roaring Lyon, chased out of the wood: and I saw that he sent out a mans voyce to the Eagle, and said,
Hear you, I will talke with you, and the highest shall say to you,
Art not you it that remain of the four beasts, whom I made to raigne in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?

And the fourth came and ouercame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fearefulnesse, and over the whole compasse of the earth with much wicked oppression, and so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit.
For the earth have you not iudged with truth.

For you have afflicted the meeke, you have hurt the peaceable, you have loued lyers, and destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit, and have cast downe the walles of such, as did you no harme.
Therefore is your wrongfull dealing come up to the Highest, and your pride to the Mighty.
The Highest also has looked upon the proud times, and behold, they are ended, and his abominations are fulfilled.
And therefore appeare no more you Eagle, nor your horrible wings, nor your wicked feathers, nor your malitious heads, nor your hurtfull clawes, nor all your vaine body:
That all the earth may be refreshed, and may returne, being deliuered from your violence, and that she may hope for the judgment, and mercy of him that made her.
And it came to pass whiles the Lyon spoke these words to the Eagle, I saw:
And behold, the head that remained, and the four wings appeared no more, and the two went to it, and set themselues up to raigne, and their kingdom was small and full of vprore.

And I saw, and behold, they appeared no more, and the whole body of the Eagle was burnt, so that the earth was in great fear: then awaked I out of the trouble and traunce of my minde, and from great fear, and said to my spirit,
Loe, this have you done to me, in that you search out the ways of the Highest.
Loe, yet am I weary in my mind, and very weake in my spirit: and litle strength is there in me; for the great fear, wherewith I was affrighted this night.
Therefore will I now beseech the Highest, that he will comfort me to the end.
And I said, Lord, that bear rule, If I have found grace before your sight, and if I am iustified with you, before many others, and if my prayer indeed be come up before your face,
Comfort me then, and show me your servant the interpretation, and plaine difference of this fearefull vision, that you maist perfectly comfort my soul.
For you have iudged me worthy, to show me the last times.
And he said to me, This is the interpretation of the vision.
The Eagle whom you sawest come up from the sea, is the kingdom which was seene, in the vision of your brother Daniel.
But it was not expounded to him, therefore now I declare it to you.
Behold, the days will come, that there shall rise up a kingdom upon earth, and it shall be feared above all the kingdoms that were before it.
In the same shall twelve kings reigne, one after another.
Whereof the second shall begin to reigne, and shall have more time then any of the twelve.
And this do the twelve wings signifie which you sawest.
As for the voice which you heard speak, and that you sawest not to go out from the heads, but from the mids of the body thereof, this is the interpretation:
That after the time of that kingdom, there shall arise great striuings, and it shall stand in perill of falling: nevertheless it shall not then fall, but shall be restored again to his beginning.
And whereas you sawest the eight small under feathers sticking to her wings, this is the interpretation:
That in him there shall arise eight kings, whose time shall be but small, and their years swift.
And two of them shall perish: the middle time approching, four shall be kept until their end begin to approch: but two shall be kept to the end.
And whereas you sawest three heads resting, this is the interpretation
In his last days shall the most High raise up three kingdoms, and renew many things therein, and they shall have the dominion of the earth,
And of those that dwell therein with much oppression, above all those that were before them: therefore are they called the heads of the Eagle.
For these are they that shall accomplish his wickednesse, and that shall finish his last end.
And whereas you sawest that the great head appeared no more, it signifies that one of them shall die upon his bed, and yet with paine.
For the two that remain, shall be slaine with the sword.
For the sword of the one shall deuoure the other: but at the last shall he fall through the sword himselfe.
And whereas you sawest two feathers under the wings passing over the head, that is on the right side:
It signifies that these are they whom the Highest has kept to their end: this is the small kingdom and full of trouble, as you sawest.
And the Lyon whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring, and speaking to the Eagle, and rebuking her for her vnrighteousnesse, with all the words which you have heard,
This is the Anointed which the Highest has kept for them, and for their wickednesse to the end: he shall reprooue them, and shall vpbraid them with their crueltie.
For he shall set them before him aliue in judgment, and shall rebuke them and correct them.

For the rest of my people shall he deliuer with mercy, those that have bin preserued upon my borders, and he shall make them ioyfull until the comming of the day of judgment, whereof I have spoken to you from the beginning.
This is the dreame that you sawest, and these are the interpretations.
You only have bene meete to know this secret of the Highest.
Therefore write all these things that you have seene, in a book, and hide them.
And teach them to the wise of the people, whose hearts you know may comprehend, and keep these seerets.
But wait you here your selfe yet seven days moe, that it may be showed you whatever it pleases the Highest to declare to you: And with that he went his way.

And it came to pass when all the people saw that the seven days were past, and I not come again into the city, they gathered them all together, from the least to the greatest, and came to me, and said,
What have we offended you? and what evil have we done against you, that you forsake us, and sit here in this place?
For of all the prophets you only art left us, as a cluster of the vintage, and as a candle in a darke place, and as a hauen or ship preserued from the tempest:
Are not the evils which are come to us, sufficient?
If you shall forsake us, how much better had it bene for us, if we also had bene burnt in the midst of Sion.
For we are not better then they that died there. And they wept with a loud voice: then answered I them, and said,
Be of good comfort, O Yahsharala, and be not heauy you house of Jacob.
For the Highest has you in remembrance, and the mighty has not forgotten you in temptation.
As for me, I have not forsaken you, neither am I departed from you: but am come into this place, to pray for the desolation of Sion, and that I might seeke mercy for the low estate of your Sanctuary.
And now go your way home every man, and after these days will I come to you.
So the people went their way into the city, like as I commanded them:
But I remained still in the field seven days, as the Angel commanded me, and did eat only in those days, of the flowers of the fielde, and ate the herbs as food.
And it came to pass after seven days, I dreamed a dreame by night.
And loe, there arose a winde from the sea that it mooued all the waues thereof.
And I beheld, and loe, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seene under him.
And whensoeuer the voyce went out of his mouth, all they burnt, that heard his voyce, like as the earth fails when it feels the fire.
And after this I beheld, and loe, there was gathered together a multitude of men out of number, from the four windes of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.
But I beheld, and loe, he had graued himselfe a great mountaine, and flew up upon it.
But I would have seene the region, or place, whereout the hill was grauen, and I could not.
And after this I beheld, and loe, all they which were gathered together to subdue him, were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.
And loe, as he saw the violence of the multitude that came, he neither lift up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war.
But only I saw that he sent out of his mouth, as it had bene a blast of fire, and out of his lippes a flaming breath, and out of his tongue he cast out sparkes and tempests,

And they were all mixt together; the blast of fire, the flaming breath, and the great tempest, and fel with violence upon the multitude, which was prepared to fight, and burnt them up every one, so that upon a sudden, of an innumerable multitude, nothing was to be perceiued, but only dust and smell of smoke: when I saw this, I was afraid.
Afterward saw I the same man come downe from the mountaine, and call to him an other peaceable multitude.
