And there came much people to him, whereof some were glad, some were sory, some of them were bound, and other some brought of them that were offred: then was I sicke through great fear, and I awaked and said,
You have showed your servant wonders from the beginning, and have counted me worthy that you should receive my prayer:
Show me now yet the interpretation of this dreame.
For as I conceiue in mine understanding, woe to them that shall be left in those days; and much more woe to them that are not left behinde.
For they that were not left, were in heauinesse.
Now understand I the things that are layde up in the latter days, which shall happen to them, and to those that are left behinde.
Therefore are they come into great perils, and many necessities, like as these dreames declare.

Yet is it easier for him that is in danger, to come into these things, then to pass away as a cloud out of the world, and not to see the things that happen in the last days. And he answered to me, and said,
The interpretation of the vision shall I show you, and I will open to you, the thing that you have required.
Wheras you have spoken of them that are left behinde, this is the interpretation.
He that shall endure the perill in that time, has kept himselfe: they that be fallen into danger, are such as have workes, and faith towards the Almightie.
Know this therefore, that they which be left behinde, are more blessed then they that be dead.
This is the meaning of the vision: Whereas you sawest a man comming up from the midst of the Sea:
The same is he whom Alahayam the highest has kept a great season, which by his own selfe shall deliuer his creature: and he shall order them that are left behinde.
And whereas you sawest, that out of his mouth there came as a blast of winde, and fire, and storme:
And that he helde neither sword, nor any instrument of war, but that the rushing in of him destroyed the whole multitude that came to subdue him, this is the interpretation.
Behold, the days come, when the most high will begin to deliuer them that are upon the earth.
And he shall come to the astonishment of them that dwell on the earth.
And one shall vndertake to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one realme against another.
And the time shalbe, when these things shall come to pass, and the signes shall happen which I showed you before, and then shall my son be declared, whom you sawest as a man ascending.
And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land, leave the battaile they have one against another.
And an innumerable multitude shalbe gathered together, as you sawest them willing to come, and to overcome him by fighting.
But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion.
And Sion shall come and shall be showed to all men, being prepared and builded, like as you sawest the hill grauen without hands.
And this my son shall rebuke the wicked inuentions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest,

And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherwith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like to a flame: and he shall destroy them without labor, by the law which is like to fire.
And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him;

Those are the ten tribes, which were caried away prisoners out of their own land, in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria ledde away captive, and he caried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.
But they tooke this counsaile amongst themselues, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go foorth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,
That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.
And they entred into Euphrates by the narrow passages of the Riuer.
For the most high then showed signes for them, and held still the flood, until they were passed over.
For through that country there was a great way to go; namely, of a year and a halfe: and the same region is called Arsareth.
Then dwelt they there until the latter time; and now when they shall begin to come,
The highest shall stay the springs of the streame again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.
But those that be left behinde of your people, are they that are found within my borders.
Now when he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he shall defend his people that remain.
And then shall he shewe them great wonders.
Then said I, O Lord, that bear rule, show me this: Why have I seene the man comming up from the midst of the Sea?
And he said to me, Like as you can neither seeke out, nor know the things that are in the deepe of the sea: even so can no man upon earth see my son, or those that be with him, but in the day time.
This is the interpretation of the dreame which you sawest, and whereby you only art here lightened.
For you have forsaken your own way, and applied your diligence to my law, and sought it.
Your life have you ordered in wisdome, and have called understanding your mother.
And therefore have I showed you the treasures of the Highest: After other three days, I will speak other things to you, and declare to you mighty and wonderous things.
Then went I forth into the field giving praise and thanks greatly to the most High, because of his wonders which he did in time,
And because he governs the same, and such things as fall in their seasons, and there I sate three days.
And it came to pass, upon the third day I sate under an oke, and behold, there came a voyce out of a bush over against me, and said, Esdras, Esdras.
And I said, Here am I Lord, and I stood up upon my feet.
Then said he to me, In the bush I did manifestly reueale my selfe to Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt.
And I sent him, and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of Sinai, where I held him by me, a long season,
And told him many wonderous things, and showed him the secrets of the times, and the end, and commanded him, saying,
These words shall you declare, and these shall you hide.
And now I say to you,
That you lay up in your heart the signes that I have showed, and the dreames that you have seene, and the interpretations which you have heard:
For you shall be taken away from all, and from henceforth you shall remain with my son, and with such as be like you, until the times be ended.
For the world has lost his youth, and the times begin to waxe old.
For the world is diuided into twelve parts, and the ten parts of it are gone already, and halfe of a tenth part.
And there remains that which is after the halfe of the tenth part.
Now therefore set your house in order, and reproue your people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption.
Let go from you mortall thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weake nature,
And set aside the thoughts that are most heauy to you, and haste you to flie from these times.
For yet greater evils then those which you have seene happen, shall be done hereafter.
For look how much the world shall be weaker through age: so much the more shall evils increase upon them that dwell therein.
For the truth is fled farre away, and leasing is hard at hand: For now hastens the vision to come, which you have seene.
Then answered I before you, and said,

Behold, Lord, I will go as you have commanded me, and reprooue the people which are present, but they that shall be borne afterward, who shall admonish them? thus the world is set in darkenes, and they that dwell therein, are without light.
For your law is burnt, therefore no man knows the things that are done of you, or the works that shall begin.

But if I have found grace before you, send the holy Ghost into me, and I shall write all that has bene done in the world, since the beginning, which were written in your Lawe, that men may find your path, and that they which will live in the latter days, may live.
And he answered me, saying, Go your way, gather the people together, and say to them, that they seeke you not for forty days.
But look you prepare you many boxe trees, and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Eranus and Asiel, these five which are ready to write swiftly.
And come here, and I shall light a candle of understanding in your heart, which shall not be put out, until the things be performed which you shall beginne to write.
And when you have done, some things shall you publish, and some things shall you show secretly to the wise: to morrowe this houre shall you beginne to write.
Then went I foorth as he commanded, and gathered all the people together, and said,
Hear these words, O Yahsharala.
Our fathers at the beginning were strangers in Egypt, from whence they were deliuered:
And received the law of life which they kept not, which you also have transgressed after them.
Then was the land, even the land of Sion, parted among you by lot, but your fathers, and you your selues have done vnrighteousnesse, and have not kept the ways which the Highest commanded you.
And for as much as he is a righteous judge, he tooke from you in time, the thing that he had given you.
And now are you here, and your brethren amongst you.
Therefore if so be that you will subdue your own understanding, and reforme your hearts, you shall be kept aliue, and after death you shall obtaine mercy.
For after death, shall the judgment come, when we shall live again: and then shall the names of the righteous be manifest, and the workes of the ungodly shall be declared.
Let no man therefore come to me now, nor seeke after me these fourty days.
So I tooke the five men as he commanded me, and we went into the field, and remained there.
And the next day behold a voyce called me saying, Esdras, open your mouth and drinke that I give you to drinke.
Then opened I my mouth, and behold, he reached me a full cup, which was full as it were with water, but the colour of it was like fire.
And I tooke it, and dranke: and when I had drunke of it, my heart uttered understanding: and wisdom grew in my brest, for my spirit strengthened my memory.
And my mouth was opened and shut no more.

The highest gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote the wonderfull visions of the night, that were told, which they knew not: And they sate fourty days, and they wrote in the day, and at night they ate bread.
As for me I spoke in the day, and held not my tongue by night:
In fourty days they wrote two hundred and four books.
And it came to pass when the fourty days were fulfilled, that the Highest spoke, saying, The first that you have written, publish openly, that the worthy and vnworthy may read it.
But keep the seuenty last, that you may deliuer them only to such as be wise, among the people.
For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountains of wisdom, and the streame of knowledge.
And I did so.
Behold, do you speak in the eares of my people the words of prophesie, which I will put in your mouth, says the Lord.
And cause them to be written in paper: for they are faithfull and true.
Fear not the imaginations against you, let not the incredulity of them trouble you, that speak against you.
For all the vnfaithfull shall die in their vnfaithfulnesse.
Behold, says the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.
For wickednesse has exceedingly polluted the whole earth, and their hurtfull workes are fulfilled.
Therefore says the Lord,

I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickednesse, which they prophanely commit, neither will I suffer them in those things, in which they wickedly exercise themselues: behold, the innocent and righteous blood cryeth to me, and the souls of the just complaine continually.
And therefore says the Lord, I will surely auenge them, and receive to me, all the innocent blood from among them.
Beholde, my people is ledde as a flocke to the slaughter: I will not suffer them now to dwel in the land of Egypt.
But I will bring them with a mighty hand, and a stretched out arm, and smite Egypt with plagues as before, and will destroy al the land thereof.
Egypt shall mourne, and the foundation of it shall be smitten with the plague and punishment, that Alahayam shall bring upon it.
They that until the ground shall mourne: for their seedes shall faile, through the blasting, and haile, and with a fearefull constellation.
Woe to the world, and them that dwell therein.
For the sword and their destruction draws near, and one people shall stand up to fight against another, and swords in their hands.
For there shalbe sedition among men, and inuading one another, they shall not regard their kings, nor princes, and the course of their actions shall stand in their power.
A man shall desire to go into a city, and shall not be able.
For because of their pride, the cities shalbe troubled, the houses shalbe destroyed, and men shalbe afraid.
A man shall have no pity upon his neighbour, but shall destroy their houses with the sword, and spoile their goods, because of the lacke of bread, and for great tribulation.

Behold, says Alahayam, I will call together all the Kings of the earth to reuerence me, which are from the rising of the Sunne, from the South, from the East, and Libanus: to turne themselues one against another, and repay the things that they have done to them.
Like as they do yet this day to my chosen, so will I do also and recompense in their bosome, Thus says the Lord Alahayam;
My right hand shall not spare the sinners, and my sword shall not cease over them, that shed innocent blood upon earth.
The fire is gone foorth from his wrath, and has consumed the foundations of the earth, and the sinners like the straw that is kindled.
Wo to them that sin and keep not my commandments, says the Lord.
I will not spare them: go your way you children from the power, defile not my Sanctuary:
For the Lord knows all them that sin against him, and therefore delivers he them to death and destruction.
For now are the plagues come upon the whole earth, and you shall remain in them, for Alahayam shall not deliuer you, because you have sinned against him.
Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the East.
Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many charets, and the multitude of them shalbe caried as the winde upon earth, that all they which hear them, may fear and tremble.

Also the Carmanians raging in wrath, shall go forth as the wilde bores of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and ioyne battell with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.
And then shall the dragons have the vpper hand, remembering their nature, and if they shall turne themselues, conspiring together in great power to persecute them,
Then these shalbe troubled, and keep silence through their power, and shall flee.
And from the land of the Assyrians, shall the enemy besiege them, and consume some of them, and in their host shall be fear, and dread and strife among their kings.
Behold clouds from the East, and from the North, to the South, and they are very horrible to look upon; full of wrath and storme.
They shall smite one upon another, and they shall smite downe a great multitude of starres upon the earth, even their own starre; and blood shalbe from the sword to the belly.
And doung of men to the camels hough.
And there shalbe great fearefulnesse and trembling upon earth: and they that see the wrath, shall be afraid, and trembling shall come upon them.
And then shall there come great stormes, from the South, and from the North, and another part from the West.
And strong winds shall arise from the East, and shall open it, and the cloud which he raised up in wrath, and the starre stirred to cause fear toward the East and West winde, shalbe destroyed.

The great and mighty cloudes shall be lifted up full of wrath, and the starre, that they may make all the earth afraid, and them that dwel therein, and they shall power out over every high and eminent place, an horrible starre.
Fire and haile, and fleeing swords, and many waters, that all fields may be full, and all riuers with the abundance of great waters.
And they shall break downe the cities, and walls, mountaines and hils, trees of the wood, and grasse of the medowes, and their corne.
And they shall go stedfastly to Babylon, and make her afraid.
They shall come to her, and besiege her, the starre and all wrath shall they power out upon her, then shall the dust and smoke go up to the heaven: and all they that be about her, shall bewaile her.
And they that remain under her, shall do seruice to them that have put her in fear.
And you Asia that art partaker of the hope of Babylon, and art the glory of her person:

Woe be to you you wretch, because you have made your selfe like to her, and have deckt your daughters in whoredome, that they might please and glory in your louers, which have alway desired to commit whordome with you.
You have followed her, that is hated in all her works and inuentions: therefore sayth Alahayam,
I will send plagues upon you: widowhood, pouertie, famine, sword, and pestilence, to waste your houses with destruction and death.
And the glory of the power shall be dried up as floure, when the heate shall arise that is sent over you.
You shall be weakened as a poor woman with stripes, and as one chastised with woundes, so that the mighty and louers shall not be able to receive you.
Would I with iealousie have so proceeded against you, says the Lord,
If you had not alway slaine my chosen, exalting the stroke of your hands, and saying over their dead, when you were drunken,
Set foorth the beauty of your countenance.
The reward of your whoredome shall be in your bosome, therefore shall you receive recompense.
Like as you have done to my chosen, sayth the Lord; even so shall Alahayam do to you, and shall deliuer you into mischiefe.
Your children shall die of hunger, and you shall fall through the sword: your cities shalbe broken downe, and all yours shall perish with the sword in the field.
They that be in the mountaines shall die of hunger, and eat their own flesh, and drinke their own blood, for very hunger of bread, and thirst of water.
You, as vnhappy, shall come through the Sea, and receive plagues again.
And in the passage, they shall rush on the idle city, and shall destroy some portion of your land, and consume part of your glory, and shall returne to Babylon that was destroyed.
And you shall be cast downe by them, as stubble, and they shall be to you as fire,
And shall consume you and your cities, your land and your mountaines, all your woods and your fruitfull trees shall they burne up with fire.
Your children shall they cary away captive, and look what you have, they shall spoile it, and marre the beauty of your face.
Woe be to you, Babylon and Asia, woe be to you Egypt and Syria.
Gird up your selues with clothes of sacke and haire, bewaile your children, and be sory, for your destruction is at hand.
A sword is sent upon you, and who may turne it backe?
A fire is sent among you, and who may quench it?
Plagues are sent to you, and what is he that may driue them away?
May any man driue away a hungry Lion in the wood? or may any one quench the fire in stubble, when it has begun to burne?
May one turne again the arrow that is shot of a strong archer?
The mighty Lord sends the plagues, and who is he that can driue them away?
A fire shall go foorth from his wrath: and who is he that may quench it?
He shall cast lightnings, and who shall not fear? he shall thunder, and who shall not be afraid?
The Lord shall threaten, and who shall not be vtterly beaten to powder at his presence?

The earth quakes and the foundations thereof, the sea arises up with waues from the deepe, and the waues of it are troubled, and the fishes thereof also before the Lord, and before the glory of his power.
For strong is his right hand that bends the bow, his arrowes that he shoots are sharpe, and shall not misse when they begin to be shot into the ends of the world.
Behold, the plagues are sent, and shall not returne again, until they come upon the earth.
The fire is kindled, and shall not be put out, until it consume the foundation of the earth.
Like as an arrow which is shot of a mighty archer returns not backward: even so the plagues that shall be sent upon earth, shall not returne again.
Woe is me, woe is me, who will deliuer me in those days?

The beginning of sorrowes, and great mournings, the beginning of famine, and great death: the beginning of warres, and the powers shall stand in fear, the beginning of evils, what shall I do when these evils shall come?
Behold, famine, and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.
But for all these things they shall not turne from their wickednes, nor be alway mindfull of the scourges.
Behold, victuals shall be so good cheape upon earth, that they shall think themselues to be in good case, and even then shall evils growe upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion.
For many of them that dwell upon earth, shall perish of famine, and the other that escape the hunger, shall the sword destroy.
And the dead shall be cast out as doung, and there shalbe no man to comfort them, for the earth shall be wasted, and the cities shall be cast downe.
There shall be no man left to until the earth, and to sow it.
The trees shall give fruit, and who shall gather them?
The grapes shall ripe, and who shall treade them? for all places shall be desolate of men.
So that one man shall desire to see another, and to hear his voyce.
For of a city there shalbe ten left, and two of the field which shall hide themselues in the thicke groues, and in the clefts of rockes.
As in an orchard of oliues, upon every tree there are left three or four oliues:
Or, when as a vineyard is gathered, there are left some clusters of them that diligently seek through the vineyard:
Even so in those days there shalbe three or four left by them that search their houses with the sword.
And the earth shall be laid waste, and the fields thereof shall waxe old, and her ways and all her paths shall grow full of thornes, because no one shall travel through it.
The virgins shall mourne having no bridegromes, the women shall mourne having no husbands, their daughters shall mourne having no helpers.
In the warres shall their bridegromes be destroyed, and their husbands shall perish of famine.
Hear now these things, and understand them, you servants of the Lord.
Behold the word of the Lord, receive it, believe not the gods of whom the Lord spoke.
Behold, the plagues draw near, and are not slacke.

As when a woman with childe in the ninth month brings forth her son, within two or three houres of her birth great paines compasse her wombe, which paines, when the child comes forth, they slacke not a moment,
Even so shall not the plagues be slacke to come upon the earth, and the world shall mourne, and sorrowes shall come upon it on every side.
O my people, Hear my word: make you ready to the battell, and in those evils, be even as pilgrimes upon the earth.
He that sells let him be as he that fleeth away: and he that buyeth, as one that will loose.
He that trades in merchandise, as he that had no profit by it: and he that builds, as he that shall not dwell therein.
He that soweth, as if he should not reape: so also he that plants the vineyard, as he that shall not gather the grapes.
They that marry, as they that shall get no children: and they that marrie not, as the widowers.
And therefore they that labor, labor in vaine.
For strangers shall reape their fruits, and spoile their goods, ouerthrowe their houses; and take their children captives, for in captiuity and famine shall they get children.
And they that occupy their merchandize with robbery, the more they decke their citties, their houses, their possessions and their own persons:
The more will I be angry with them for their sin, says the Lord.
Like as an whore envies a right honest and vertuous woman:
So shall righteousness have iniquity, when she decks herselfe, and shall accuse her, to her face, when he comes that shall defend him that diligently searches out every sin upon earth.
And therfore be you not like therunto, nor to the workes thereof.
For yet a little iniquitie shall be taken away out of the earth, and righteousness shall reigne among you.
Let not the sinner say that he has not sinned: for Alahayam shall burne coales of fire upon his head, which says before the Lord Alahayam and his glory, I have not sinned.
Behold, the Lord knows all the workes of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts:
Which spoke but the word, let the earth be made, and it was made: let the heaven be made, and it was created.
In his word were the starres made, and he knows the number of them.
He searches the deepe, and the treasures thereof, he has measured the Sea, and what it contains.
He has shut the Sea in the midst of the waters, and with his word has he hanged the earth upon the waters.
He spreads out the heavens like a vault, upon the waters has he founded it.
In the desart has he made springs of water, and pooles upon the tops of the mountaines, that the floods might power downe from the high rockes to water the earth.
He made man, and put his heart in the midst of the body, and gave him breath, life, and understanding.
Yea and the spirit of Almighty Alahayam, which made all things, and searches out all hidden things in the secrets of the earth.
Surely he knows your inuentions, and what you thinke in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.
Therefore has the Lord exactly searched out all your workes, and he will put you all to shame.
And when your sins are brought foorth you shalbe ashamed before men, and your own sins shall be your accusers in that day.
What will you do? or how will you hide your sins before Alahayam and his Angels?

Behold, Alahayam himselfe is the judge, fear him: leave off from your sins, and forget your iniquities to medle no more with them for ever, so shall Alahayam do you lead forth, and deliuer you from all trouble.
For behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you, and they shall take away certaine of you, and feede you being idle with things offered to idoles.
And they that consent to them shall be had in derision, and in reproch, and troden under foote.
For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.
They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.
For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.
Then shall they be known who are my chosen, and they shall be tried, as the gold in the fire:
Hear, O you my beloued, says the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliuer you from the same.
Be you not afraid, neither doubt, for Alahayam is your guide,
And the guide of them who keep my commandments, and precepts, says the Lord Alahayam; Let not your sins weigh you downe, and let not your iniquities lift up themselues.

Woe be to them that are bound with their sins, and couered with their iniquities: like as a field is couered over with bushes, and the path thereof couered with thornes, that no man may trauell through.
It is left vndressed, and is cast into the fire, to be consumed therewith.
